Definition: a ram (as full-grown and fat), including a battering-ram (as butting); hence, a meadow (as for sheep); also a pad or camel's saddle (as puffed out)
BiblicalUsage: Kar is the ram — full-grown and fat, the pride of the flock and the measure of wealth, and by extension the battering-ram that breaks a wall. Saul spared the best of the sheep and the fatlings; Mesha of Moab rendered a hundred thousand rams to the king of Israel; Amos rebukes those who eat the lambs out of the flock; and Ezekiel is told to set battering rams against the city.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the ram holds both pictures at once: the fat of the flock that men spare for themselves, and the ram that breaks the wall. What we keep back for ourselves becomes the thing that breaks us — and that is why Saul's sparing was his undoing.
